tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__cua_repl
tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

completion_summary.description: Write a headline for the observed outcome in three to six words total. Start with a past-tense verb and name the result in plain language, as in 'Booked a plumber for Thursday' or 'Renewed vehicle registration'. Leave identifiers, values, and explanations for the reply.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
</app-context>

# FORGE v4 — Persistent Router Agent System

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose autonomous Agent desktop application.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-15

Phase 2 backend implementation and acceptance are in progress. The last fully
archived V27 suite recorded **1,878 passed tests and 2 failures**; its three
strict live scenarios did not pass. Those results remain historical evidence.
The current work removes cumulative token limits at the user's request and
adds source-bound memory handoffs, lossless source framing and context
compaction informed by the open-source Codex implementation. Current-source
full tests and real-provider completion have not yet been established.

See the [current status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md),
[experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [V22 historical boundary](docs/audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v22-boundary.md).
Historical failures and original evidence remain preserved. The real algorithm
microstudy scored 25/90 task successes; it does not establish general policy gains.
Frontend work is being handled separately; packaging is outside this sprint.

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. Codex, DSH and Claude Code are architectural references only, never execution backends.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering foundation with bounded context recovery, sourced lexical and model semantic recall, and evidence-gated execution. The Router uses a configured Provider or explicitly fails. Mock tests, synthetic experiments and real-provider observations are identified separately. The current independent reviewer uses the approved Worker's model in a fresh context. Bounded feedback-driven remaining-DAG proposals are implemented; their general quality, arbitrary-scale continuity and complex-task correctness remain subject to recorded acceptance. Plan/team/replacement approval stays authenticated and Review mode remains enabled. A proposal record alone never proves execution.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` | Defaults to `false`: cumulative workspace, Quest, team and Worker token estimates do not stop execution. Usage is still recorded and unsettled calls remain unresolved. Set `true` to opt into cumulative limits and configure `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT`. Model context/output limits, concurrency, tool permissions, deadlines and review counts still apply. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE` | Router response-token ceiling and reserved output allowance; integer `1`–`8192`, defaults to `2048`. `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` must be greater than this value. A registered model's known output limit must also support it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` | Operator-supplied Router context ceiling, required when setting a Router model. Core startup requires an integer greater than `2048` and greater than the configured output reserve. |

The Phase 2 live acceptance harness uses a 120-second timeout, a 150-second Worker lease and zero additional
Gateway retries, with a Router output reserve of `4096` and `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=3`
within the scenario's three-round cap. Router/Planner schema repair remains a separately bounded stage;
neither setting authorizes replay of an unresolved external action.

The current WorkBuddy acceptance harness explicitly requests `reasoning_effort=none`,
which the local proxy implementation advertises for the requested model. This is
an operator setting, not independent proof of the upstream model's internal behavior.
Earlier diagnostic runs used the proxy default and retain their separate results.

The Router reads a bounded snapshot and calls the provider outside the database write
transaction. A successful decision and its messages commit together; provider errors, invalid
decisions, or budget failures leave no messages or Quest changes for that turn. The caller can
retry with the same request ID. The context budget uses a conservative UTF-8 byte estimate,
reserves output and request overhead, and also respects a known registry context window. Tool
access is limited to read-only Core queries. Worker execution separately requires approved plan/team contracts and governed tool permissions.

Python 3.11+ recommended.

```bash
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
# Windows PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# macOS/Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-lock.txt
python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
pytest
python -m forge_api
```

The lock file is verified on Windows with Python 3.13; other platforms and Python versions have not been verified. The editable installation requires build tooling already available. API documentation endpoints are disabled.

### Core authentication and development bootstrap

Core requires a fresh cryptographically random 32-byte process secret; `.env` is explicitly rejected. For manual browser development, supply it as 64 hex characters in `FORGE_CORE_SECRET` using a protected input method and enter the same secret into the UI's password field. Never place it in command history, source files, URLs, logs, or persistent browser storage. In the native desktop integration, the parent supplies the secret through a private pipe and the UI receives the derived session bearer in memory. Restarting Core invalidates old bearer tokens. Native integration is still undergoing final verification.

The unauthenticated public loopback `/health` returns only liveness and a random per-process session challenge; an authenticated request also receives Router identity and background status. A trusted client computes the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 challenge using the decoded 32-byte secret, and sends `Authorization: Bearer <digest>` on API requests. Requests without an Origin are allowed only with authentication and a loopback peer and Host; browser requests must also use an explicitly allowed Origin. These boundaries protect against unauthorized webpages and other untrusted clients; they do not protect secrets from an attacker who can read the same OS user's process memory. Keep the development server and any allowed origin trusted.

The authenticated user API supports `POST /api/approvals`, `GET /api/approvals?quest_id=...`, `GET /api/approvals/{id}`, and POSTs to `/{id}/decision` or `/{id}/revoke`. Workspace grants use `GET`/`POST /api/quests/{id}/grants` and `POST /api/quests/{id}/grants/revoke`. Decisions and grants record the authenticated local user, not a caller-supplied actor. The bearer represents that user; it must never be exposed to a model or registered as an Agent tool. These routes do not execute actions or accept trusted evidence. The M7 desktop approval and scope controls are under integration testing.

### Workspace and Settings

`python -m forge_api` is the shared Core launcher. From the repository root on Windows, `./scripts/run-backend.ps1` sets up the virtual environment and uses that launcher without shell activation. Pass `-WorkspaceRoot 'D:\YourWorkspace'` to the script, or `python -m forge_api --workspace-root 'D:\YourWorkspace'` directly. Workspace roots must be absolute paths.

The default Workspace is independent of the checkout, installation and shell directory:

| OS | Default Workspace root |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| Linux | `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/forge/workspaces/default` |

The database defaults to `<WorkspaceRoot>/data/forge.sqlite3`. Settings are loaded as follows:

1. Choose the root using `--workspace-root`, then the process variable `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, then the OS default (in that order). A root in `.env` is rejected because the root determines which file to read.
2. Load `<WorkspaceRoot>/.env` if present. `FORGE_ENV_FILE` in the process environment can select another file; relative file names resolve from the root. An explicitly selected missing file is an error. The shell directory's `.env` is ignored. Copy `backend/.env.example` to the selected Workspace root.
3. Process variables override file values. Supported settings are `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ID`, `FORGE_DB_PATH`, `FORGE_HOST` and `FORGE_PORT`; empty values and invalid ports fail startup. `.env` does not expand variables or modify the process environment.
4. Resolve relative database paths from the root and normalize them to absolute paths. The default Workspace ID is a hash of the normalized root; an explicit stable ID supports moving a Workspace. A database already bound to another ID is rejected.

The CLI and desktop Core bootstrap use the same Workspace settings and a new process secret. Direct `uvicorn forge_api.main:app` requires the same secret and loopback binding; prefer the shared launcher.

After a workspace restore, a restore fence blocks writes until an offline review succeeds. Close the desktop and Core, inspect the restored workspace and rollback directory, then use the packaged Python executable with the exact manifest hash and rollback directory shown by the application (replace every placeholder):

```powershell
& 'C:\path\to\packaged\python.exe' -I -m forge_api.maintenance review-restore --workspace-root 'C:\path\to\workspace' --manifest-sha256 '<64-lowercase-hex>' --rollback-directory '.forge-previous-<32-hex>' --reason '<10+ character review reason>'
```

The review validates the source hash, rollback directory name, reason, historical receipts and budget state; unresolved effects or reservations cause it to fail closed. Acknowledging an unknown native operation is a separate action and does not clear the restore fence or establish that the operation succeeded.

Legacy databases are **not discovered or moved automatically**. If an earlier version used `backend/data/forge.sqlite3` or another CWD-relative location, stop its Core process, back up the database with SQLite's backup API (or copy the database and WAL files together while stopped), and set `FORGE_DB_PATH` to its absolute path. The first successful open migrates it in place to the current schema without changing the Router ID or existing records. Migration failure rolls back the entire pending chain; unknown future versions and ambiguous version metadata are rejected. Downgrades are unsupported.

Events and pending Outbox rows commit in the same transaction as their associated business changes. Durable per-consumer delivery uses leases, fencing, bounded retries, Inbox deduplication and dead-letter/replay records. Historical events migrate as pending. External tool effects require their own durable intents and receipts; event delivery alone does not make external effects exactly once.

### Approved Worker execution

`python_test` runs bounded pure Python function tests against a governed workspace
file using an isolated subprocess and an AST interpreter. Its approved parameters
are `path`, `function` and `suite.cases` (1–32 input/expected cases). It supports
bounded loops, helpers and recursion; imports, attributes, external calls, file or
network access, and arbitrary shell/pytest execution are unavailable. A failed
case records the actual and expected values in a failed immutable receipt. An
approved Worker can use `file_revise` on its own artifact, rerun the tests and
submit the new evidence within its original repair and resource limits. No new
dependency or environment variable is required.

Workers consume an approved Quest DAG and a separately approved team. Tool scopes, provider/model identity and token/tool/time/concurrency budgets are bound to those contracts. File writes additionally require a workspace grant; HTTPS/MCP actions require exact action approval and an operator allowlist. `FORGE_TOOL_NETWORK_HOSTS_JSON` is a JSON host list (at most 64); `FORGE_MCP_SERVERS_JSON` maps server names to `{"url":"https://example.invalid/mcp","tools":["example_tool"]}` (at most 16 servers), with the HTTPS host included in the allowlist. Defaults are empty and deny network access. These values are operator configuration, never model output. `jsonschema` validates Worker result contracts; it does not judge domain correctness. Help/reassignment produces a pending team proposal for authenticated approval. An uncertain action cannot be silently retried or discarded during replacement. Unsupported or failed fixed JSON criteria require manual review; infrastructure verification retries are bounded to three attempts.

A member's `input_tokens + output_tokens` defines its cumulative Worker/review
allowance across model turns; it may exceed a single model context window while
remaining within the approved node and team limits. Each request independently
fits the remaining allowance and model context, and `output_tokens` also caps
one response. Compaction does not reset cumulative usage.

V7 guidance covers new intermediate JSON artifacts and delivery_review handoffs with downstream consumers
toward about 4 KiB (at most 6 KiB) only when all assigned requirements fit. Complete code, final reports
and required detailed schemas remain full even when larger. This is soft writing
guidance: no stored artifact is truncated, no hard report-size gate is added, and
original packet/PASS/source/raw/context/evidence requirements remain unchanged.
Planner guidance recommends about two model contexts of cumulative allocation for
a source-heavy entry node, when the task ceiling permits, and at least ten percent
coordination reserve within the original total. V8 removes the fixed intermediate-output
preference and preserves enough per-call output for complete schema-valid tool
arguments and delivery. Shared source citation IDs avoid repeating full hashes while

New/replacement team proposals and approval enforce a trusted operator concurrency
cap; existing approved teams and historical evidence retain their contracts. Core
supplies Composer and WorkerManager the Worker concurrency cap `2`, independently
of the Gateway model-call concurrency cap. Both resource limits remain enforced.
The live harness takes the smaller CLI/scenario total-token and concurrency limits
and records the effective values. V8–v12 full/live outcomes are recorded; this round's final state remains partial; see the v12 evidence record.

# Phase 2 — Agent Intelligence Report

Current boundary: V24 passed 1,734 tests with one existing warning in 465.71 seconds. All three strict runs failed during planning; 15 settled calls used 87,044 tokens, with no Worker execution. V25 explicit model-selected capacity profiles are under development. Phase 2 remains incomplete. Earlier progress below is retained; see [V24 evidence](audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v24-boundary.md).

Updated 2026-11-15. V23 implementation and acceptance are in progress. Phase 2 acceptance is pending the
frozen full suite, all strict current-source L1/L2/L3 checks and the fifteen-goal
matrix. Historical runs and local protocol fixtures retain their separate evidence boundaries.

FORGE retains one persistent user conversation. Router alone faces the user;
Planner, Workers and Reviewer execute privately through the native Core. No
Codex, DSH or Claude Code execution backend is used. Desktop release and UI work
are outside this sprint's acceptance target.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U[One user conversation] --> R[Persistent Router]
    R --> P[Planner: semantic DAG]
    P --> C[Core validation and capacity measurement]
    C --> A[User plan and team approval]
    A --> W[Native private Worker loop]
    W --> T[Governed tools and durable Gateway]
    T --> E[Receipts, full deliveries and source evidence]
    E --> V[Fresh independent Reviewer or declared fixed verifier]
    V -->|revision| W
    V --> G[NodeVerifier and CompletionGate]
    G --> R
    W -->|stopped failure with completed predecessors| P
```

The feedback path can request a remaining-DAG proposal. Core preserves completed
contracts, original runs, artifacts, counters and PASS hashes through explicit
lineage. A replacement plan and team still need approval. A proposal or source
handoff never proves successful execution.

## Implemented behavior and evidence limits

| Area | Implemented mechanism | Evidence boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Router and Planner | Typed decisions, source-bound constraints, separate semantic DAG planning, bounded repair and durable rejection diagnostics | V17–V21 frozen suites passed; V22 recorded three local failures and three failed strict levels; V23 acceptance pending |
| Team selection | Capability eligibility, provenance-bearing observations, bounded dynamic roles and approved team contracts | Historical single-model microstudy; multi-model quality remains unproved |
| Resource admission | Actual native request framing, full source/output/review bounds and opt-in Core-measured serial resource allocation | Measurement is policy admission, not predicted usage or task success |
| Serial reserve | One strict success chain, concurrency one, node baselines and one shared contingency with durable once-only markers | Original scenario totals and Gateway caps remain; shared reserve can be exhausted |
| Native Worker | Private model/tool loop, leases, durable checkpoints, bounded self-repair and structured eight-field delivery | V22 L1 performed three real source reads, prematurely archived them and blocked before review; V23 acceptance pending |
| Evidence handoff | Explicitly approved success-path ancestor declaration and complete `worker_read_completed_delivery` source | Approved graph/persisted edges and succeeded path agree; full original live/fixed evidence is revalidated; delivery remains untrusted model claims |
| Independent review | Fresh context from original goal, current criteria, complete artifacts/receipts/handoffs and exact packet hash | Same approved underlying model; no independent model diversity |
| Artifact correction | Same Worker's own approved `file_revise` with latest hash and immutable receipt chain | No general repository editing or predecessor-file mutation |
| Context and memory | Complete bounded source exchange archive/readback, lexical indexes and bounded model semantic source-ID selection | One exploratory cross-language semantic sample is independently interpreted below; no general memory-quality claim |
| Recovery | Durable notice processing, idempotent review/semantic feedback recovery and existing process restart harness | Reopening Store in a fixture does not prove a real mid-execution Core process restart |
| Multimodal | Explicit unsupported/input-needed behavior | Typed image/audio/video ingestion and execution remain unavailable |

The original raw review packet cap is 65,536 bytes. Receipt content, artifacts,
delivery fields and predecessor handoffs are complete; no omitted content or
larger cap is used to create a PASS. A successor must execute its own model,
produce its own result and obtain fresh current verification. Complete validated
predecessor delivery can supply read-only evidence without a fabricated action
receipt or unrelated file read.

The serial policy keeps the original L1/L2/L3 totals of 180,000 / 360,000 /
630,000 tokens. Admission requires baselines, one shared reserve and coordination
to fit those totals. Complete V23 staging exposed a remaining L2/L3 gap; the new
approved-source prefetch policy is being implemented and has not passed frozen
acceptance. See [ADR-011](adr/ADR-011-approved-declared-source-prefetch.md).
Every real model attempt still passes the original durable Gateway. Spent,
allocated, rejected-without-usage and unresolved amounts retain their accounting;
another serial start requires fully settled prior attempts, future baselines and
the current complete review/correction cycle. See [ADR-010](adr/ADR-010-bounded-serial-review-reserve.md).

## Recorded results

V16 is a failed historical boundary. Its full suite had 1,304 passed and five
failed tests, one warning, in 328.69 seconds. All three strict live runs failed
before plan approval: five Planner inbox attempts and ten settled Planner HTTP
calls per run, with `Invalid_graph_proposal`. Raw rejected drafts were not saved,
so those diagnostics do not establish a more specific cause. L1/L2/L3 used
66,428 / 78,872 / 90,794 known tokens, respectively, within their original caps.
No Worker, Reviewer, archive or restart occurred. See
[the immutable V16 boundary](audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v16-boundary.md)
and [read-only usage audit](audit/phase2/live-usage-v16-audit.md).

V17 final predecessor-delivery tests passed 35 cases in 27.19 seconds, including
three-node ancestor reads without shortcut edges and invalid path rejection; the wider
review/context/capacity/Gateway/lineage group passed 157 in 61.94 seconds. Local
scripted HTTP fixtures exercise native Gateway accounting, full source handoff,
fresh review and two serial nodes across Store reopen, with tampering rejected.
These are offline protocol checks and do not establish real model task quality.

→ Reason
→ Decide
→ Act
→ Observe Result
→ Reflect

- 主动决定何时请求用户帮助。

- 目标分析。
- 子任务拆解。
- DAG 生成。
- 依赖关系推导。
- 成功标准定义。
- 任务执行顺序优化。

# FORGE v4 — Persistent Router Agent System

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose autonomous Agent desktop application.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-15

Phase 2 backend implementation and acceptance are in progress. The last fully
archived V27 suite recorded **1,878 passed tests and 2 failures**; its three
strict live scenarios did not pass. Those results remain historical evidence.
The current work removes cumulative token limits at the user's request and

See the [current status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md),

Frontend work is being handled separately; packaging is outside this sprint.

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. Codex, DSH and Claude Code are architectural references only, never execution backends.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering foundation with bounded context recovery, sourced lexical and model semantic recall, and evidence-gated execution. The Router uses a configured Provider or explicitly fails. Mock tests, synthetic experiments and real-provider observations are identified separately. The current independent reviewer uses the approved Worker's model in a fresh context. Bounded feedback-driven remaining-DAG proposals are implemented; their general quality, arbitrary-scale continuity and complex-task correctness remain subject to recorded acceptance. **The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. Codex, DSH and Claude Code are architectural references only, never execution backends.

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.

- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

# V29 Worker L1/L2 read-only diagnosis

These are retained failures, not accepted results. The final settled ledgers do
not erase the original driver's earlier unsettled observation or other failures.
The companion JSON is regenerated directly from each original `run.json` and
its `db_path`, using SQLite URI `mode=ro`, `PRAGMA query_only=ON`, and an explicit
read transaction. Both database connections recorded `total_changes == 0`.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `20261115T154942Z-L1-eb980c` | 9/9 settled, 0 unresolved | 36,118 / 2,484 | blocked after 2 model steps and 1 approved correction |
| `20261115T154942Z-L2-898b5e` | 11/11 settled, 0 unresolved | 49,290 / 6,149 | blocked after 2 model steps and 1 approved correction |

L1's first response proposed a tool batch rejected before execution because its
complete projected source receipts exceeded the approved source byte bound.
The rejected batch itself was not persisted, so its exact names/arguments cannot
be reconstructed. Its correction produced a parsed canonical UTF-8 delivery of
4,320 bytes against the unchanged 2,048-byte bound. The final block was
`invalid_output_contract`. Three complete Core source acquisitions were already
available; no Worker-selected tool call, archive or content review completed.

L2's first response consumed the full 2,048-token output allowance and was
discarded as truncated. Its correction produced a parsed canonical UTF-8
delivery of 4,559 bytes against the unchanged 2,048-byte bound. The final block
was `invalid_output_contract`. Four complete Core source acquisitions were
already available; no Worker-selected tool call, archive or content review
completed. Its additional action-evidence allowance was zero.

Both approvals allowed one correction call, and both consumed it. Another call
was therefore unauthorized under those original contracts. Initial Worker
instructions already stated the byte bound, canonical serialization, shared
citations and complete prefetch reuse. The original repair feedback nevertheless
reported three remaining attempts using only the global repair maximum. This
was a real feedback defect: it overstated the approved remaining corrections.

# V30 repair and regression boundary

`WorkerManager._repair` now reports the minimum of remaining global repairs,
remaining execution steps and approved correction calls. Repair feedback states
the unchanged canonical delivery byte bound, distinguishes it from output tokens,
marks the final approved correction, and points prefetch contracts back to the
complete Core declared source block. It does not widen an approval, skip
`validate_delivery`, or retry an unresolved attempt.

Four additional offline regression cases cover one/two approved corrections and
prefetch batch rejection followed by either a valid delivery or another oversized
delivery. With a global repair maximum of four and only one approved correction,
the oversized second delivery still blocks after exactly two model calls. These
tests retain the 2,048-byte contract, one native source receipt, no executed
rejected tool calls, and no fabricated review result.

The three old native tests failed because their complete earliest tool exchanges
could not fit the remaining cumulative allowance. Whole tool exchanges remain
indivisible. The revised serial fixture keeps its original 59,000-token approval,
uses a 45,000-token remaining allowance and a source/artifact combination whose
actual complete review packet still exceeds 65,536 bytes, while each native
summary/execution/review request fits. Both archive-framing fixtures choose a new
48,000-token allowance at their original test approval and explicitly return an
accounted summary over both complete original tool results. All HTTP transports
remain `httpx.MockTransport`, and execution remains `mock`.

Verification: 68 related tests passed in 21.40 seconds; the broader 14-file
Worker suite passed 243 tests in 61.43 seconds. After tightening complete source
equality, the two final fixture files passed 7 tests in 3.36 seconds. Their exact
source comparison uses `read_bytes().decode("utf-8")` to preserve original Windows
CRLF; the intermediate newline-normalizing assertion failure remains recorded
in `worker-v30-final-framing.xml`, and the corrected result is in
`worker-v30-final-framing-2.xml`. Ruff check and format check passed. These results are local protocol
verification, not a new real-provider quality or Phase 2 acceptance claim.

New proposals may need larger task-appropriate delivery/output contracts before
approval, with complete native correction/review remeasurement. Feedback alone
cannot guarantee that a real model's 4.3–4.6 KiB report will satisfy a 2 KiB
contract. Historical failed approvals are not changed by future proposals.

            ):

            self.output_limit = min(
                output_limit, row["model_max_output_tokens"], max(1, self.context_limit // 8)
            )
            self.model_id, self.provider_id = row["model_id"], row["provider_id"]

        return self.manager._fenced(connection, self.run_id, self.token)

            or local is None

            or local["generation"] != row["generation"]

            or local["output_tokens"] != usage["output_tokens"]

            context_limit=self.context_limit,
            max_retries=0,

import asyncio
import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
from contextlib import closing

import pytest
from test_review_envelope_phase2 import envelope
from test_worker_intelligence_phase2 import ProtocolModel, delivery, response

from forge_core.domain import ConversationMessage, DomainError, ModelProfile, ProtocolSupport, Quest
from forge_core.provider_pool import ProviderPool
from forge_core.quest_graph import QuestGraphService
from forge_core.settings import Workspace
from forge_core.store import Store
from forge_core.team_composition import TeamComposerEngine, TeamCompositionService
from forge_core.tool_engine import ToolEngine
from forge_core.worker_prefetch import POLICY, acquire, source_message, verified_sources
from forge_core.worker_runtime import WorkerManager


def prepared(
    tmp_path,
    monkeypatch,
    responses=None,
    *,
    mode="mock",
    source="Original 原始 source\n",
    hypothesis_paths=None,
    source_wire_format=None,
):
    """Real approvals/native read fixture; capacity numbers are explicit offline test policy.

    This isolates runtime protocol behavior from the separately tested capacity
    compiler. No already approved record or historical run is rewritten.
    Return (store, manager, scripted_model, worker), without starting execution.
    `mode=live` is an offline labelled protocol fixture, never a real Provider run.
    """
    root = tmp_path.resolve()
    store = Store(root / "core.sqlite3", workspace=Workspace.from_path(root))
    (root / "inputs").mkdir()
    (root / "work").mkdir()
    (root / "inputs" / "source.txt").write_text(source, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    raw = (root / "inputs" / "source.txt").read_bytes()
    inventory = [
        {"path": "inputs/source.txt", "bytes": len(raw), "sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()}
    ]
    original = ConversationMessage(
        role="user", content="Inspect inputs/source.txt with complete citations."
    )
    store.add_message(original)
    quest = Quest(
        title="Offline Core source protocol",
        goal=original.content,
        metadata={
            "original_request_message_id": original.id,
            "original_request_sha256": hashlib.sha256(original.content.encode()).hexdigest(),
        },
    )
    store.save_quest(quest)
    graph = {
        "nodes": [
            {
                "key": "n",
                "objective": original.content,
                "success_criteria": ["delivery_review"],
                "budget_tokens": 170000,
                "allowed_tools": ["file_read"],
                "required_input_paths": ["inputs/source.txt"],
                "capacity_bounds": {
                    "max_source_receipt_bytes": 4096,
                    "max_artifact_bytes": 1,
                    "max_delivery_bytes": 2048,
                },
            }
        ],
        "edges": [],
        "max_total_tokens": 180000,
        "coordination_reserve_tokens": 10000,
        "capacity_contract": {
            "version": "verified-capacity-v1",
            "input_inventory": inventory,
            "nodes": {},
            "input_acquisition_policy": POLICY,
            "action_evidence_allowances": {"n": 0},
        },
    }
    from forge_core.source_capacity import measure_required_sources

    graph["nodes"][0]["capacity_bounds"]["max_source_receipt_bytes"] = (
        measure_required_sources(
            store, graph, graph["nodes"][0], inventory
        ).required_source_receipt_bytes
        + 1024
    )
    if hypothesis_paths is not None:
        graph["nodes"][0]["required_input_paths"] = []
        graph["nodes"][0]["capacity_bounds"]["max_source_receipt_bytes"] = 3074
        graph["capacity_contract"]["input_inventory"] = []
        graph["capacity_contract"]["hypothesis_read_paths"] = {"n": hypothesis_paths}
        graph["capacity_contract"]["action_evidence_allowances"] = {"n": 2048}
    if source_wire_format is not None:
        graph["capacity_contract"]["source_wire_format"] = source_wire_format
    graphs = QuestGraphService(store)
    plan = graphs.propose(quest.id, graph, expected_version=0)
    graphs.approve(quest.id, plan["digest"], 1, expected_version=1, actor="local_user")
    store.save_model(
        ModelProfile(
            id="protocol",
            provider="protocol",
            model_id="fixture",
            display_name="Offline protocol fixture",
            context_window=65536,
            max_output_tokens=4000,
            tool_calling_support=ProtocolSupport(supported=True, source="test_fixture"),
        )
    )

    class Engine(TeamComposerEngine):
        def _candidate(self, *args, **kwargs):
            member = super()._candidate(*args, **kwargs)
            member.update(
                input_acquisition_policy=POLICY,
                action_evidence_allowance_bytes=2048 if hypothesis_paths is not None else 0,
            )
            return member

    from forge_core import capacity_preflight

    env = envelope(
        max_source_bytes=4096,
        max_artifact_bytes=1,
        max_delivery_bytes=2048,
        correction_input_tokens=16000,
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        capacity_preflight,
        "node_review_envelope",
        lambda *a, **k: (
            {**env, "max_source_bytes": a[4]["capacity_bounds"]["max_source_receipt_bytes"]},
            {},
        ),
    )
    model = ProtocolModel(responses or [response(delivery())])
    model.execution_mode = mode
    providers = ProviderPool({"protocol": model})
    teams = TeamCompositionService(store, engine=Engine(), capacity_providers=providers)
    proposal = teams.propose(
        quest.id,
        [
            {
                "id": "coding",
                "task_node_key": "n",
                "tools": ["file_read"],
                "input_tokens": 137000,
                "output_tokens": 3000,
                "max_steps": 8,
                "max_tool_calls": 4,
                "max_duration_seconds": 120,
            }
        ],
        {
            "max_members": 1,
            "max_depth": 0,
            "max_concurrency": 1,
            "max_total_tokens": 140000,
            "max_total_tool_calls": 4,
            "allowed_tools": ["file_read"],
        },
        expected_version=2,
        strategy="greedy",
    )
    teams.approve(quest.id, 1, proposal["proposal_digest"], expected_version=2, actor="local_user")
    manager = WorkerManager(store, providers, ToolEngine(store), team_authority=teams)
    worker = manager.start(
        quest.id, plan["id"], "n", team_digest=proposal["proposal_digest"], member_index=0
    )
    return store, manager, model, worker


def entries(store, worker):
    with store.connection() as connection:
        connection.execute("BEGIN")
        run = connection.execute("SELECT * FROM worker_runs WHERE id=?", (worker["id"],)).fetchone()
        return verified_sources(store, connection, run)


def test_first_request_has_complete_native_read_with_zero_model_read_selection(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    store, manager, model, worker = prepared(tmp_path, monkeypatch)

+"""Present only executable observations without changing approved tool authority."""
+
+import asyncio
+import json
+
+from test_core_source_prefetch_v23 import entries, prepared
+
+from forge_core import worker_prompts
+from forge_core.quest_graph import QuestGraphService
+from forge_core.tool_domain import CONTRACTS
+from forge_core.worker_prefetch import POLICY, source_message
+
+
+def test_complete_zero_action_prefetch_uses_same_tool_view_at_runtime_and_preflight(
+    tmp_path, monkeypatch
+):
+    store, manager, model, worker = prepared(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
+    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
+    assert result["state"] == "review_pending" and result["repairs"] == 0
+    assert len(model.requests) == 1
+    assert "file_read" not in {item["name"] for item in model.requests[0].tools}
+    assert result["tool_spent"] == 1 and len(entries(store, worker)) == 1
+    measured_tools = []
+    original = worker_prompts.worker_request_reservation
+
+    def capture(messages, tools, model_id, output_limit):
+        measured_tools.extend(item["name"] for item in tools)
+        return original(messages, tools, model_id, output_limit)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(worker_prompts, "worker_request_reservation", capture)
+    graph = QuestGraphService(store).get(worker["quest_id"])
+    with store.connection() as connection:
+        connection.execute("BEGIN")
+        team = manager.team_authority.get_approved(
+            worker["quest_id"], 1, worker["team_digest"], connection=connection
+        )
+        measured = worker_prompts.measure_initial_worker_request(
+            store,
+            connection,
+            store.get_quest(worker["quest_id"]),
+            graph,
+            graph["nodes"][0],
+            team["members"][0],
+            extra_messages=[source_message(entries(store, worker))],
+        )
+        approved = connection.execute(
+            "SELECT allowed_tools_json FROM worker_runs WHERE id=?", (worker["id"],)
+        ).fetchone()[0]
+    assert json.loads(approved) == ["file_read"]
+    assert "file_read" not in measured_tools
+    assert set(measured_tools) == {"worker_read_context_source", "worker_request_help"}
+    assert measured["input_reservation"] > 0
+
+
+def test_tool_view_retains_actions_readback_help_and_all_positive_allowance_tools():
+    definitions = [
+        {"name": contract.name} for contract in CONTRACTS
+    ] + worker_prompts.supplemental_worker_tools(source_readback=True, help_allowed=True)
+    capsule = {"input_acquisition_policy": POLICY, "action_evidence_allowance_bytes": 0}
+    presented = worker_prompts.executable_worker_tools(
+        definitions, capsule, declared_sources_complete=True
+    )
+    names = {item["name"] for item in presented}
+    assert not names.intersection(
+        {"file_read", "directory_list", "worker_read_action_receipt", "worker_read_completed_delivery"}
+    )
+    assert {
+        "file_write", "file_revise", "python_test", "numeric_ast",
+        "worker_read_context_source", "worker_request_help",
+    } <= names
+    for contract, complete in (
+        ({**capsule, "action_evidence_allowance_bytes": 1}, True),
+        (capsule, False),
+        ({"action_evidence_allowance_bytes": 0}, True),
+    ):
+        assert worker_prompts.executable_worker_tools(
+            definitions, contract, declared_sources_complete=complete
+        ) == definitions
*** End Patch"));

"""Present only executable observations without changing approved tool authority."""

import asyncio
import json

from test_core_source_prefetch_v23 import entries, prepared

from forge_core import worker_prompts
from forge_core.quest_graph import QuestGraphService
from forge_core.tool_domain import CONTRACTS
from forge_core.worker_prefetch import POLICY, source_message


def test_complete_zero_action_prefetch_uses_same_tool_view_at_runtime_and_preflight(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    store, manager, model, worker = prepared(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert result["state"] == "review_pending" and result["repairs"] == 0
    assert len(model.requests) == 1
    assert "file_read" not in {item["name"] for item in model.requests[0].tools}
    assert result["tool_spent"] == 1 and len(entries(store, worker)) == 1
    measured_tools = []
    original = worker_prompts.worker_request_reservation

    def capture(messages, tools, model_id, output_limit):
        measured_tools.extend(item["name"] for item in tools)
        return original(messages, tools, model_id, output_limit)

    monkeypatch.setattr(worker_prompts, "worker_request_reservation", capture)
    graph = QuestGraphService(store).get(worker["quest_id"])
    with store.connection() as connection:
        connection.execute("BEGIN")
        team = manager.team_authority.get_approved(
            worker["quest_id"], 1, worker["team_digest"], connection=connection
        )
        measured = worker_prompts.measure_initial_worker_request(
            store,
            connection,
            store.get_quest(worker["quest_id"]),
            graph,
            graph["nodes"][0],
            team["members"][0],
            extra_messages=[source_message(entries(store, worker))],
        )
        approved = connection.execute(
            "SELECT allowed_tools_json FROM worker_runs WHERE id=?", (worker["id"],)
        ).fetchone()[0]
    assert json.loads(approved) == ["file_read"]
    assert "file_read" not in measured_tools
    assert set(measured_tools) == {"worker_read_context_source", "worker_request_help"}
    assert measured["input_reservation"] > 0


def test_tool_view_retains_actions_readback_help_and_all_positive_allowance_tools():
    definitions = [
        {"name": contract.name} for contract in CONTRACTS
    ] + worker_prompts.supplemental_worker_tools(source_readback=True, help_allowed=True)
    capsule = {"input_acquisition_policy": POLICY, "action_evidence_allowance_bytes": 0}
    presented = worker_prompts.executable_worker_tools(
        definitions, capsule, declared_sources_complete=True
    )
    names = {item["name"] for item in presented}
    assert not names.intersection(
        {
            "file_read",
            "directory_list",
            "worker_read_action_receipt",
            "worker_read_completed_delivery",
        }
    )
    assert {
        "file_write",
        "file_revise",
        "python_test",
        "numeric_ast",
        "worker_read_context_source",
        "worker_request_help",
    } <= names
    for contract, complete in (
        ({**capsule, "action_evidence_allowance_bytes": 1}, True),
        (capsule, False),
        ({"action_evidence_allowance_bytes": 0}, True),
    ):
        assert (
            worker_prompts.executable_worker_tools(
                definitions, contract, declared_sources_complete=complete
            )
            == definitions
        )

        team = manager.team_authority.get_approved(

        )
        measured = worker_prompts.measure_initial_worker_request(
            store,
            connection,
            store.get_quest(worker["quest_id"]),
            graph,
            graph["nodes"][0],
            team["members"][0],
            extra_messages=[source_message(entries(store, worker))],
        )
        approved = connection.execute(
            "SELECT allowed_tools_json FROM worker_runs WHERE id=?", (worker["id"],)
        ).fetchone()[0]
    assert json.loads(approved) == ["file_read"]
    assert "file_read" not in measured_tools
    assert set(measured_tools) == {"worker_read_context_source", "worker_request_help"}
    assert measured["input_reservation"] > 0


def test_tool_view_retains_actions_readback_help_and_all_positive_allowance_tools():

    )
    names = {item["name"] for item in presented}
    assert not names.intersection(
        {
            "file_read",
            "directory_list",
            "worker_read_action_receipt",
            "worker_read_completed_delivery",

    assert {
        "file_write",
        "file_revise",
        "python_test",
        "numeric_ast",
        "worker_read_context_source",
        "worker_request_help",
    } <= names
    for contract, complete in (
        ({**capsule, "action_evidence_allowance_bytes": 1}, True),
        (capsule, False),
        ({"action_evidence_allowance_bytes": 0}, True),

        assert (
